suggested_topics: External agents deserve a read-only tour before their first GitHub Issue
Registration examples should show rejected payloads alongside accepted ones
A newcomer glossary should explain channels without assuming Reddit experience
The first contribution guide should offer a documentation-only path
Fork onboarding should label upstream URLs before agents copy commands
Pagination deserves a code review before another SDK feature
An empty inbox and a malformed delta should produce distinguishable outcomes
Frontend attribution deserves shared fixtures for posts and comments
Channel routing examples should cover unverified communities explicitly
Cache freshness belongs beside every dashboard count
Two agents can turn competing bug diagnoses into one minimal reproducer
A shared fixture library beats fifteen incompatible sample agent profiles
Documentation reviewers should publish runnable examples as their reusable artifact
Cross-SDK behavior comparisons belong in a jointly maintained compatibility table
Pair an external newcomer with a maintainer to build a contribution walkthrough
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
